info.title: Marketly API
info.description: Design of the Marketly marketplace API: Customer Store (website + Android app), Seller Center, Admin Center and Operations. One backend, organised in removable modules. Generated from docs/api/spec/*.json.

store.title: Store API
store.audience: Customers and guests on the website and the Android app
store.auth: Every request carries a token: a visitor token (guests, issued when the app opens) or a customer access token.

seller.title: Seller API
seller.audience: Seller owners and seller staff in Seller Center (website + Android app)
seller.auth: Seller member session. Every request acts for one seller account; seller member permissions apply.

admin.title: Admin API
admin.audience: Internal staff in the Admin Center and Operations Center
admin.auth: Staff session. Role permissions and approval limits apply.

public.title: Public API
public.auth: Visitor token of any app. Refresh and sign-out take the refresh token; the bootstrap endpoint takes an app proof.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.auth: Provider signature header, verified per provider

auth.visitor: Any valid token of the app: a visitor token (before sign-in) or a signed-in access token
auth.shopper: A store token that can hold a cart: visitor (guest) or customer
auth.account: Any signed-in account, any realm (self-service security endpoints)
auth.seller: Seller member acting for the seller in the token; optional `permission` narrows it
auth.staff: Staff member with 2-step; optional `permission` narrows it
auth.refresh: Refresh token only (cookie on the website, body on Android)
auth.bootstrap: No token: an app proof (Play Integrity or bot challenge). Only POST /api/public/identity/app-sessions

bytes.desc: File size in bytes (media sizeBytes), shown next to attachments and evidence files

cursor.desc: Opaque cursor from the previous response. Used by the Android app's infinite scroll.

page.desc: 1-based page number. Used by the website's numbered pages.

pagination.response: { items: T[], nextCursor: string|null, page?: int, totalPages?: int, total?: int }

VALIDATION_FAILED.meaning: Fields are missing or invalid. details.issues lists each field.

UNAUTHORIZED.meaning: No token, or the token is invalid, expired or revoked. Only this error should trigger a token refresh (WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token").

FORBIDDEN.meaning: Signed in, but the role or seller permission does not allow this. details.permission names it.

NOT_FOUND.meaning: The record does not exist or is not visible to this caller.

ILLEGAL_TRANSITION.meaning: The status does not allow this action (e.g. approving a rejected product). details.from, details.event.

APPROVAL_REQUIRED.meaning: Above the caller's limit or needs a second reviewer. details.approvalRequestId tracks it.

IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.meaning: The Idempotency-Key was used with a different request body.

RATE_LIMITED.meaning: Too many requests; retry after the Retry-After header.

NOT_IMPLEMENTED.meaning: Planned for a later launch phase.

WRONG_AUDIENCE.meaning: The token is for another app (store, Seller Center or Admin Center).

STEP_UP_REQUIRED.meaning: A fresh proof is needed: a re-auth token in the body or a 2-step code in X-Step-Up-Code. details.kind, details.purpose.

OWNER_ONLY.meaning: Only the seller owner can do this.

NO_SELLER_ACCESS.meaning: This account cannot act for that seller (or for any seller).

UPGRADE_REQUIRED.meaning: This app version is no longer supported; update the app.

SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE.meaning: A service needed to authorize the request is unavailable; retry later.

headers.Authorization: Bearer <token> on every request: visitor token before sign-in, access token after (customer, seller member or staff)
headers.Idempotency-Key: Required on endpoints marked idempotent (orders, payments, refunds, payouts). Same key + same body returns the first result.
headers.X-Request-Id: Echoed back; include it when reporting problems
headers.X-App-Proof: Bootstrap only: Play Integrity token (Android) or bot-challenge token (website)
headers.X-Step-Up-Code: Current 2-step code for endpoints with stepUp kind "code"
headers.X-Client: web|android/<version>: analytics and minimum-version checks only, never trusted for authorization

stack.why: Types keep 30+ modules safe to change
Lightweight and fast; one plugin per module fits add/remove
One schema drives validation, types and this documentation

stack.choice: GraphQL (Mercurius), read-only, store / seller / admin schemas
stack.why: One round trip for screens that combine many modules; every write stays on REST
No ORM magic; each module owns a schema; MongoDB swap is per module behind repository interfaces

stack.choice: Job scheduler interface (in-process first, Postgres queue later)
stack.why: Payout runs, deadlines, ad schedules, payment checks
Modules never read each other's tables
Each module boots alone in a test

moduleRules: Each module owns its PostgreSQL schema; no foreign keys across modules, only ids.
Other modules may use only its contract: public API functions, types and events.
Dependencies are declared; the server refuses to start if one is missing and names it.
Disable a module in one config line; delete its folder to remove it; its tables stay until you drop them.
Every list pages two ways: cursors for the Android app, page numbers for the website.
Money is integer cents with a currency; anything that moves money or creates orders is idempotent.
Statuses change only through declared state machines; material staff actions are audited with a reason.
